user.title: ZoneFlow Irrigation
user.description: Give this irrigation zone a short name (e.g. "Front Lawn", "Avocado Tree"). To add more zones later, add this integration again.

data_description.zone_name: Becomes the zone's device name and the start of its entity names, and shows in phone messages. E.g. "Tomato bed", "Front lawn".
data_description.plant: Fills in sensible starting values for this crop: weekly water targets, crop factor, deep soak and growth ramp. "Something else" starts from general values. You can change all of them later on the zone's device page.
data_description.zone_type: Outdoor is how ZoneFlow has always worked. Greenhouse and indoor zones add climate control (fans, vents, misting, heater), can work without a valve, and have no rain gauge or forecast because of the roof.
data_description.start_from: Start from a copy of another zone's watering settings or a saved preset instead of the plant type's. Valve, sensors and flow rate are never copied.
data_description.location: The area this zone is in, if any. It then uses the area's rain gauge, temperature sensor, weather and phone unless you give it its own.
data_description.quick_setup: Asks only for the valve and how the water is delivered, and fills in the rest from the plant type and the sensors ZoneFlow found. You can change everything later in Configure. Untick to see every setting now.

entities.title: ZoneFlow Irrigation

data.soil_type: Do you know your soil type? (skip if not)
data.drainage: Does water drain away slowly? (skip if you do not know)
data.slope: Is the ground sloped? (skip if it is flat or you are not sure)
data.irrigation_method: How does the water get to the plants?
data.growth_ramp_profile: Is it a young plant that needs less water at first? (skip if not)

data_description.valve_entity: The switch that opens this zone's valve (or starts its pump). The only thing ZoneFlow can't work without: it switches it on and off, and always makes sure it ends up off.
data_description.pump_power_entity: A power sensor (W) on the pump, e.g. from a smart plug. During each watering ZoneFlow checks that the pump really draws power, and warns you if it doesn't. Leave empty if you don't have one.
data_description.pump_id: Only for zones that run from the same pump: give them all the same name here (any name, e.g. "Pump A") and they take turns instead of running at the same time. Leave empty if this zone has its own pump or water supply.
data_description.rain_counter_entity: Your rain gauge sensor: a tip counter, a rain total in millimetres or a rain rate (choose which just below). ZoneFlow then subtracts rain from what it waters, lets wet soil dry out first, and stops a watering when it starts raining. Without a gauge, ZoneFlow waters as if it never rains.
data_description.rain_source_type: What that sensor reports. Tip counter: a count that goes up by one with every tip of the bucket (set the size of a tip on the zone's device page, Rain Gauge mm per Tip). Rain total in mm: a running total that only goes up, or one that starts again every day or week, for example from Ecowitt, Ambient Weather or Tempest (a total in inches works too). Rain rate: the current rain in mm per hour, which ZoneFlow adds up over time (less exact). A sensor that shows only the last hour or the last 24 hours does not work: use a total. Changing the sensor or the type starts the rain history again. Rain per reading: the amount that fell since the previous update, for example the Tempest Precipitation sensor, which ZoneFlow adds up.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: An outdoor temperature sensor. With it, ZoneFlow waters more in hot weather and less in cool weather by itself, and the frost guard holds watering off when it's freezing. Without it, the Fallback / Manual Temperature setting decides.
data_description.flow_meter_entity: A water meter that counts up the total volume (litres, gallons or m³). ZoneFlow then logs how much water each watering really used, warns you if the pump ran but no water moved, and can measure the flow rate for you (Configure → Flow rate).
data_description.soil_moisture_entity: A soil moisture sensor (%) in this zone's root zone. Dry soil brings the routine watering forward, wet soil skips it, and in between the normal schedule decides. The dry and wet levels are on the zone's device page.
data_description.notify_entity: Your phone's notify entity from the Home Assistant Companion app. ZoneFlow sends faults and notable events there, and the weekly summary if you turn it on. Without one, they only go to the log.
data_description.weather_entity: A weather entity with a forecast. ZoneFlow holds a watering off when enough rain is forecast (but not for too many days in a row), and uses its current temperature for the frost guard when there's no temperature sensor.
data_description.soil_type: Decides how each watering is split into pulses, so the water soaks in instead of running off: about 3 mm per pulse on clay, 15 mm on loam, 30 mm on sand, with a 30-minute soak between pulses (an hour on clay and clay loam). "Not sure" uses a cautious middle value. You can also change it later on the zone's device page.
data_description.drainage: Slow-draining soil (a hard, compact layer underneath) takes less water per pulse and gets an hour's soak between pulses.
data_description.slope: Water runs off a slope before it soaks in: a moderate slope adds one pulse to each watering, a steep one two.
data_description.irrigation_method: How the water is delivered. With drip or a soaker hose on sandy soil a new zone starts with at least two pulses, so the water stays in the root zone. How much water it gives is set by the flow rate (Configure → Flow rate).
data_description.growth_ramp_profile: Gives young plants less water and grows it to the full weekly target as they get older, counted from the Planting / Transplant Date on the zone's device page. Off: always the full target. Custom: draw your own curve on the device page.
data_description.csv_path: A file where every watering, skip and warning is written with its numbers, for checking what ZoneFlow did (opens in any spreadsheet). The suggested file in your config folder is fine.
data_description.deep_soak_enabled: A deep soak is a big, slow watering every couple of weeks (14 days to start with) that wets the soil deep down, so roots grow deep. Good for trees, shrubs and perennials; turn it off for shallow-rooted plants like salad and herbs. The routine watering runs either way.
data_description.deep_soak_time: When the deep soak starts on the days it's due, when its trigger below is the fixed time. Early morning is best: less water lost to sun and wind.
data_description.routine_time: When ZoneFlow checks each day whether the routine watering is due, and waters if it is. How often it's due follows the weather and your weekly target. Early morning is best.
data_description.deep_soak_sun_mode: Start the deep soak at the fixed time above, or before or after sunrise or sunset, so it moves with the seasons.
data_description.deep_soak_sun_offset_minutes: How many minutes before or after sunrise or sunset. Not used with the fixed time.
data_description.routine_sun_mode: Start the routine watering at the fixed time above, or before or after sunrise or sunset, so it moves with the seasons.
data_description.routine_sun_offset_minutes: How many minutes before or after sunrise or sunset. Not used with the fixed time.
data_description.unit_system: What this zone shows: follow Home Assistant, or always metric (mm, °C, litres) or imperial (inches, °F, gallons). It only changes what you see, never how much it waters.

climate.title: Climate
climate.description:
{progress}

What is the growing season like where this zone is? This only pre-fills the temperature sliders on the next page -- you can change every value there, and later on the zone's device page.

data_description.climate: Pick the closest match. It only fills in the temperature thresholds on the next page.

temperatures.title: Temperature thresholds

data_description.hot_temp_threshold: When the average of the last 3 days' highs is at or above this, the zone uses its Hot weekly target and waters more often.
data_description.cool_temp_threshold: When that average is below this, the zone uses its Cool weekly target. In between is normal weather.
data_description.fallback_temp: Used when there's no real reading. Without a temperature sensor this is your manual control: raise it for a heat wave, lower it for a cold spell.

greenhouse_devices.title: Climate devices and sensors
greenhouse_devices.description: Point this at your real sensors and devices. All are optional, but a fan, vent, mister or heater needs the inside temperature sensor. You can add or change them later under Configure.

data_description.inside_temp_entity: The temperature sensor inside the greenhouse or room. Needed for any fan, vent, mister or heater, and used for watering too.
data_description.inside_humidity_entity: A humidity sensor inside. Lets ZoneFlow vent or mist by humidity and stop misting when it is damp enough.
data_description.light_entity: A light sensor (lux or solar radiation). Can start misting on bright days.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: A temperature sensor outside. With it, ZoneFlow only ventilates to cool when the outside air is cooler than inside, so it never pulls hotter air in. Without it, it works from the inside readings only.
data_description.fan_entities: Fans that cool or exhaust. Any switch, input boolean or fan. They all switch together.
data_description.vent_entities: Roof or side vents: covers, or switches that open them. They all move together.
data_description.mister_entities: Misters or foggers: a switch or valve. ZoneFlow runs them in short pulses and always makes sure they end up off.
data_description.heater_entities: Heaters: a switch, or a climate entity. Switched on when it gets too cold.
data_description.notify_entity: A phone notification target for warnings, such as a failed sensor. Leave empty for none.
data_description.unit_system: Show temperatures in Celsius or Fahrenheit. Automatic follows Home Assistant.
data_description.backup_temp_entities: Optional, recommended for a greenhouse with a heater. Extra temperature sensors inside, best placed away from the main one. If the main sensor stops working, control carries on with the first backup that works, and you get a message.

water_valve.title: Does this zone water?
water_valve.description: Pick the valve switch if this zone waters its plants. Leave it empty for a climate-only zone (then it needs at least one device).

data_description.valve_entity: The switch that opens this zone's valve. Leave empty for a climate-only zone that doesn't water.

weather_underground.title: Weather Underground rain (experimental)
weather_underground.description:
Borrows rain readings from private weather stations near your garden, for outdoor zones WITHOUT a rain gauge. Have a rain gauge? You don't need this.

**First**, check the map on wunderground.com for stations within a few km of your garden that report rain. If there are none, stop here.

**Second**, the free API key needs a station of your own: register one on wunderground.com and upload at least outdoor temperature and humidity (for example with the ha-weather-uploader integration). The API key is then in your Weather Underground account.

The readings are only used for rain deduction. They are not 100 % accurate, and less so the further the stations are from your zones.

data_description.api_key: From your Weather Underground account (API Keys). Stored only in this entry.
data_description.radius_km: 0.5-2 km, nearer is better: rain can differ a lot over a couple of km. Over 1 km, keep an eye on how the readings match the rain at your place.

wu_stations.title: Pick 1-3 stations
wu_stations.description: Stations within the radius, nearest first, with today's rain. Pick up to 3. With 3, ZoneFlow uses the middle reading; with 2, the lower one; 1 station works but is less reliable. For stations over 1 km away, compare their readings with the rain at your place for a while before trusting them.

data_description.stations: Up to 3. Check that each station's rain today looks right before you trust it.

crop.title: Add a crop to a greenhouse
crop.description: A crop is its own watering zone inside a greenhouse: its own valve, soil probe and schedule. It uses the greenhouse's inside sensors and climate.

crop_valve.description: The valve that waters this crop.

area.description: A part of the garden, for example Backyard or Front yard. Its zones use the sensors set here, unless a zone has its own.

data_description.area_rain_mm_per_tip: Only for a tip counter: how many mm of rain one tip is.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Optional. Sets the hot / cool watering tier for the zones of this area.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Lets the zones of this area skip watering when rain is forecast.
data_description.notify_entity: Optional. Where the zones of this area send their phone messages.
data_description.area_name: What the area is called, for example Backyard or Front yard.

flow_rate.title: Emitter flow rate
flow_rate.description: How much water the zone's emitters put on the area they wet. 1 litre on 1 m² is 1 mm. This assumes every emitter on the zone's valve gives the same flow. For drippers at single plants, use the area around them that actually gets wet. The result replaces the zone's Emitter Flow Rate Calibration. With mixed emitters, measure instead ("Flow rate: measure it by the litres a service run gives"). It also sets Zone Flow, the litres per minute used for the water-use estimate.

data.emitters: Number of emitters (drippers, sprayers) in the zone

data_description.emitters: Count every dripper or sprayer this zone's valve feeds.
data_description.emitter_flow: What one emitter gives per hour: it's printed on the emitter or its packaging (e.g. 2 L/h, 0.5 gal/h).
data_description.area: The area that actually gets wet. For drippers at single plants, add up the wet patches around them, not the whole bed.

flow_measure.title: Measure the flow rate
flow_measure.description: Runs the valve for {minutes} minutes as a service run (not counted as watering, but its minutes count toward today's runtime safety cap) and works the flow rate out from the flow meter's litres. The meter must only measure this zone's water while it runs. The result comes as a phone message and is set automatically; switching Service Mode off cancels it.

data_description.area: The area the zone's emitters actually wet. For drippers at single plants, add up the wet patches around them, not the whole bed.

data_description.drainage: Slow-draining soil (a hard, compact layer underneath) takes less water per pulse and gets an hour's soak between pulses.
data_description.slope: Water runs off a slope before it soaks in: a moderate slope adds one pulse to each watering, a steep one two.
data_description.irrigation_method: How the water is delivered. With drip or a soaker hose on sandy soil a new zone starts with at least two pulses, so the water stays in the root zone. How much water it gives is set by the flow rate (Configure → Flow rate).
data_description.growth_ramp_profile: Gives young plants less water and grows it to the full weekly target as they get older, counted from the Planting / Transplant Date on the zone's device page. Off: always the full target. Custom: draw your own curve on the device page.
data_description.deep_soak_enabled: A deep soak is a big, slow watering every couple of weeks (14 days to start with) that wets the soil deep down, so roots grow deep. Good for trees, shrubs and perennials; turn it off for shallow-rooted plants like salad and herbs. The routine watering runs either way.
data_description.deep_soak_time: When the deep soak starts on the days it's due, when its trigger below is the fixed time. Early morning is best: less water lost to sun and wind.
data_description.routine_time: When ZoneFlow checks each day whether the routine watering is due, and waters if it is. How often it's due follows the weather and your weekly target. Early morning is best.
data_description.deep_soak_sun_mode: Start the deep soak at the fixed time above, or before or after sunrise or sunset, so it moves with the seasons.
data_description.deep_soak_sun_offset_minutes: How many minutes before or after sunrise or sunset. Not used with the fixed time.
data_description.routine_sun_mode: Start the routine watering at the fixed time above, or before or after sunrise or sunset, so it moves with the seasons.
data_description.routine_sun_offset_minutes: How many minutes before or after sunrise or sunset. Not used with the fixed time.

wu_key.title: Weather Underground rain (experimental)
wu_key.description:
Borrows rain readings from private weather stations near your garden, for outdoor zones WITHOUT a rain gauge. Have a rain gauge? You don't need this.

**First**, check the map on wunderground.com for stations within a few km of your garden that report rain. If there are none, stop here.

**Second**, the free API key needs a station of your own: register one on wunderground.com and upload at least outdoor temperature and humidity (for example with the ha-weather-uploader integration). The API key is then in your Weather Underground account.

The readings are only used for rain deduction. They are not 100 % accurate, and less so the further the stations are from your zones.

data_description.api_key: From your Weather Underground account (API Keys). Stored only in this entry.
data_description.radius_km: 0.5-2 km, nearer is better: rain can differ a lot over a couple of km. Over 1 km, keep an eye on how the readings match the rain at your place.

wu_stations.title: Pick 1-3 stations
wu_stations.description: Stations within the radius, nearest first, with today's rain. Pick up to 3. With 3, ZoneFlow uses the middle reading; with 2, the lower one; 1 station works but is less reliable. For stations over 1 km away, compare their readings with the rain at your place for a while before trusting them.

data_description.stations: Up to 3. Check that each station's rain today looks right before you trust it.

weather_underground.title: Weather Underground rain
weather_underground.description: Use the rain from the Weather Underground stations for this zone (it has no rain gauge). Experimental: not 100 % accurate.

data_description.use_weather_underground: Only for zones without a rain gauge. Set up the Weather Underground entry first.

crop_valve.title: Crop valve
crop_valve.description: The valve that waters this crop.

data_description.valve_entity: A switch that opens this crop's water. Each crop needs its own valve.

flow_volume.title: Measure the flow rate by volume
flow_volume.description:
Press one of the zone's Service Run buttons (a longer run, such as 15 min, is more accurate) and catch or read the water: a bucket or barrel at the emitters, or the difference on a water meter. Then enter the minutes the valve was open, the litres, and the area the emitters wet. 

The result is the zone's AVERAGE: litres divided by area and minutes, and it replaces the zone's Emitter Flow Rate Calibration. ZoneFlow has one rate per zone, so it cannot tell emitters apart. For a precise result, every emitter on a zone's valve should be the same type and flow; put different emitters on separate valves (separate zones). On a mixed zone the plants on the weaker emitters get less than the average shown. It also sets Zone Flow, the litres per minute used for the water-use estimate.

data_description.minutes: The Service Run's length, as pressed (1, 5, 10 or 15 min).
data_description.volume: All the water the zone's emitters gave during the run (litres, or gallons in US units).
data_description.area: The area that actually gets wet. For drippers at single plants, add up the wet patches around them, not the whole bed.

zone_flow.title: Zone flow
zone_flow.description: The zone's total flow, from its heads. ZoneFlow multiplies it by the valve's open minutes to estimate the litres used (shown as Water Used and under the last watering). It does not change how much or when the zone waters; that is the Emitter Flow Rate Calibration. Drippers are usually rated per hour, sprinklers per minute. For the most accurate figure, measure it instead: the menu entry about the litres a service run gave also sets this.

data.heads: Number of heads (drippers, sprinklers) on the zone's valve

data_description.heads: Count every head this valve feeds.
data_description.head_flow: What one head gives, from its package or nozzle chart.
data_description.head_flow_unit: The unit the flow of one head is given in.

location.title: Where is this?
location.description: The area or greenhouse this zone is in. A zone uses the sensors of its area unless it has its own. In a greenhouse it is a crop of it. Choose New area to make an area from this zone's own sensors.

data_description.location: An area, a greenhouse, or none. Moving the zone restarts it so it reads the new place's sensors.

location_sensors.title: Use the area's sensors?
location_sensors.description: This zone has its own sensor where the area has a different one. Tick to use the area's; untick to keep the zone's own.

data_description.rain_counter_entity: Tick to use the area's rain gauge instead of this zone's own.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Tick to use the area's outdoor temperature sensor instead of this zone's own.
data_description.weather_entity: Tick to use the area's weather entity instead of this zone's own.
data_description.notify_entity: Tick to send to the area's phone instead of this zone's own.

new_area.title: New area
new_area.description: An area made from this zone's sensors. The zone moves into it, and other zones can join it later.

data_description.rain_counter_entity: Optional. The zones of this area read their rain from it unless a zone has its own gauge.
data_description.area_rain_mm_per_tip: Only for a tip counter: how many mm of rain one tip is.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Optional. Sets the hot / cool watering tier for the zones of this area.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Lets the zones of this area skip watering when rain is forecast.
data_description.notify_entity: Optional. Where the zones of this area send their phone messages.
data_description.area_name: What the area is called, for example Backyard or Front yard.
data_description.rain_source_type: What the rain gauge sensor reports: a tip counter, a rain total, a rain rate, or the rain since the last reading.

area_settings.title: Area
area_settings.description: The name of the area and the sensors its zones share. A zone with its own sensor keeps using that.

data_description.rain_counter_entity: Optional. The zones of this area read their rain from it unless a zone has its own gauge.
data_description.area_rain_mm_per_tip: Only for a tip counter: how many mm of rain one tip is.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Optional. Sets the hot / cool watering tier for the zones of this area.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Lets the zones of this area skip watering when rain is forecast.
data_description.notify_entity: Optional. Where the zones of this area send their phone messages.
data_description.area_name: What the area is called, for example Backyard or Front yard.
data_description.rain_source_type: What the rain gauge sensor reports: a tip counter, a rain total, a rain rate, or the rain since the last reading.

abort.flow_rate_out_of_range: That works out to {rate}, outside what the setting allows ({low} to {high}). Check the numbers -- for drippers spaced around single plants, use the area they actually wet, not the whole bed.
abort.measuring: Measuring: the valve runs for about {minutes} minutes. The result comes as a phone message (or in Home Assistant's notifications if the zone has no phone target) and is set automatically.
abort.zone_not_loaded: This zone isn't running right now, so this can't be done.
abort.zone_busy: The zone (or its pump) is busy, or today's runtime safety cap is used up. Try again later.
abort.flow_rate_disabled: The zone's Emitter Flow Rate Calibration entity is disabled. Enable it (the zone's device page → its entities) and try again.
abort.zone_flow_set: Zone flow set to {flow}. It is used for the water-use estimate only.
abort.zone_flow_out_of_range: That works out to a zone flow outside what the setting allows (0 to 2000 L/min). Check the numbers.

options.fixed: Use the fixed clock time above

options.established_perennial: Establishing perennial (e.g. a young tree or shrub)

options.tropical: Tropical (hot all year, e.g. Southeast Asia)

options.custom: Something else (I'll set it up myself)

options.amount_mm: Rain per reading (mm or in; e.g. Tempest)

state.full_dose_no_temp: Full dose today (no temperature reading on record)

state.established_perennial: Establishing perennial (e.g. a young tree or shrub)

state.outside: Part of the time while cold outside

run_deep_soak.description: Runs the deep-soak cycle now if (and only if) the same gates the 05:00 schedule uses are satisfied (mutex free, 14-day interval + dry-down met, 14-day rain ceiling not exceeded). Identical code path to the scheduled run.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity

run_routine_irrigation.name: Run Routine Irrigation
run_routine_irrigation.description: Runs the routine irrigation cycle now if (and only if) the same gates the 05:30 schedule uses are satisfied. Identical code path to the scheduled run.

device_id.name: Zone Device

entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

snooze_today.name: Snooze Today
snooze_today.description: Skips whichever of this zone's scheduled cycles (deep soak, routine, or both) hasn't already run today, without changing any other setting. Normal scheduling resumes automatically starting tomorrow.

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone's device. Only needed with 2+ zones configured.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

test_pulse.name: Test Pulse
test_pulse.description: Bypasses every schedule/dry-down/rain gate and runs one short valve pulse, for bench-testing the valve/pump wiring before trusting the real schedule. Still respects the mutex lock and safety watchdogs.

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone's device. Only needed with 2+ zones configured.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

send_weekly_summary.name: Send Weekly Summary Now
send_weekly_summary.description: Sends the weekly summary now to every phone that has a zone with a Weekly Summary day set -- a preview; the week's counts carry on until the scheduled one.

add_rain.name: Add Rain
add_rain.description: Records rain read by hand from a simple rain gauge. It counts like gauge rain for the rain credit, deep soak and the dry-down, but not for the 30-minute "raining now" checks. On a zone with its own rain gauge the higher of the two counts, never the sum.

amount.name: Amount
amount.description: Rain in the zone's units (mm, or inches on an imperial zone).

when.name: When
when.description: When the rain fell (default now). At most 14 days back.

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone's device. Only needed with 2+ zones configured.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

create_area.name: Create Area
create_area.description: Makes a new area (a part of the garden such as Backyard). Target a zone and it moves into the new area, which starts with that zone's rain gauge, outdoor temperature, weather and phone settings.

name.name: Name
name.description: What the area is called, for example Backyard or Front yard.

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone to put in the new area (optional).

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to that zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

add_plant.name: Add Plant
add_plant.description: Adds a plant to a zone. In a zone with no main plant it becomes the main plant and its type's settings go onto the zone; otherwise it is a record only (history, notes), unless Old Main Plant says it takes over.

plant_type.name: Plant Type
plant_type.description: Starting settings for this kind of plant (custom if left out).

old_main.name: Old Main Plant
old_main.description: Only when the zone already has a main plant. What becomes of it: keep it there as a record or archive it.

ready_days.name: Ready After Days
ready_days.description: Follow this plant as a nursery plant: it is ready to move this many days after planting (0 = do not follow). Leave out to not follow it.

planted.name: Planted
planted.description: The day it was planted (for the ready-to-move count).

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone. Only needed with 2+ zones configured.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

move_plant.name: Move Plant
move_plant.description: Moves a plant, with its history, to another zone. Its settings go onto the zone it arrives in.

plant_id.name: Plant
plant_id.description: The plant's id (shown in the zone's Status attributes).

old_main.name: Old Main Plant
old_main.description: Only when the zone already has a main plant. What becomes of it: keep it there as a record, archive it, swap it to the zone this plant leaves, or keep this plant as a record only.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

remove_plant.name: Remove Plant
remove_plant.description: Takes a plant out of its zone. It stays on record with its history. The next plant in the zone becomes the main plant.

set_main_plant.name: Set Main Plant
set_main_plant.description: Makes a plant the main plant of its zone: its settings go onto the zone and the old main plant stays as a record.

add_plant_note.name: Add Plant Note
add_plant_note.description: Adds a note to a plant's history.

set_plant_ready.name: Set Plant Ready To Move
set_plant_ready.description: Follows a nursery plant towards "ready to move": ready this many days after it was planted. A phone message says when it is. 0 stops following it; leaving the days out uses the usual number for its type.

ready_days.name: Ready After Days
ready_days.description: Days after planting (0 = stop following it).

save_preset.name: Save Preset
save_preset.description: Saves a zone's watering settings (not its valve, sensors, flow rate, planting date or notes) under a name, to start other zones from. The same name replaces the preset.

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone. Only needed with 2+ zones configured.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

copy_settings.name: Copy Settings
copy_settings.description: Gives a zone another zone's watering settings, or a saved preset's. Not the valve, sensors, flow rate, planting date or notes.

source_device_id.name: Copy From Zone
source_device_id.description: The zone to copy the settings from (or choose a preset).

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: The name of a saved preset (or choose a zone to copy from).

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone that gets the settings.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

water_now.name: Water Now
water_now.description: Waters the zone by hand for a number of minutes. Not while the zone is paused, never longer than the zone's Routine Max Safety Runtime Cap, and inside the day's runtime cap. Counts in the water record (litres), but does not move the routine or deep soak schedule.

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone. Only needed with 2+ zones configured.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

calibrate_flow.name: Calibrate Flow Rate
calibrate_flow.description: Sets the flow rate from a measured run: the water that came out (collected in a bucket or read from a water meter), the area it fell on, and how long the valve was open. Also sets Zone Flow, for litres.

volume.name: Water
volume.description: How much water came out (litres, or gallons on an imperial zone).

area.name: Area
area.description: The area that water fell on (m2, or ft2 on an imperial zone).

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: How long the valve was open.

device_id.name: Zone Device
device_id.description: The zone. Only needed with 2+ zones configured.

entity_id.name: Zone Entity
entity_id.description: Any entity belonging to the zone's device (alternative to Zone Device).

date_in_future.message: This date can't be in the future: it records something that already happened. Only the Planting / Transplant Date may be set ahead.

cool_not_below_hot.message: The cool weather threshold has to stay below the hot weather threshold. To move both down, lower the cool one first; to move both up, raise the hot one first.

zone_busy.message: This zone is busy (watering or already running a service run). Try again when it's finished.

pump_busy.message: The pump this zone shares is in use by another zone right now. Try again when that zone has finished.

daily_cap_reached.message: This zone has reached today's maximum runtime safety cap, so no service run can start until tomorrow (or raise the Max Daily Irrigation Runtime cap).

zone_paused.message: This zone is paused. Switch Pause off to water it.

pause_until_past.message: Pick a date and time in the future to pause until.

no_weekly_summary.message: No zone has a Weekly Summary day and a phone notify target set, so there's nothing to send.

summary_send_failed.message: The weekly summary couldn't be sent: the phone notification failed. Check the zone's notify target.

zone_has_no_valve.message: This zone has no valve, so it can't water. Add a valve under Configure if you want it to.

manual_rain_zero.message: Set the Manual Rain amount above 0 first.

manual_rain_not_outdoor.message: Manual rain is only for outdoor zones.

manual_rain_future.message: Rain can't be entered for a time in the future.

manual_rain_too_old.message: Rain can be entered at most 14 days back.

nothing_on_hold.message: Nothing is on hold: every device is already under ZoneFlow's control.

location_not_available.message: That place is not available any more.

greenhouse_cannot_be_crop.message: A greenhouse with climate devices cannot be a crop of another greenhouse.

area_name_exists.message: An area with this name already exists.

plant_same_zone.message: The plant is already in that zone.

plant_old_main_choice.message: {zone} already has a main plant. Say what becomes of it (Old Main Plant).

plant_zone_has_no_valve.message: Only a zone with a valve can have a main plant.

preset_not_found.message: There is no preset with that name.

copy_same_zone.message: Choose a different zone to copy from.

copy_source_required.message: Choose a zone or a preset to copy from.

water_now_out_of_range.message: Water for at least 1 minute and at most {max} minutes (this zone's safety cap).

calibration_out_of_range.message: Those numbers give a flow rate this zone cannot have. Check the water, the area and the minutes.

calibration_unavailable.message: This zone has no flow rate setting to calibrate.

plant_ready_days_range.message: Choose 1 to {max} days (or 0 to stop following the plant).

valve_unavailable.title: {zone}: valve unavailable
valve_unavailable.description: The valve of zone {zone} ({entity}) has been unavailable for over an hour, so the zone can't water. Check the valve's device and its integration. This clears by itself once the valve is back.

shared_valve.title: {zone}: valve shared with another zone
shared_valve.description: Zone {zone} and zone {other_zone} are both configured with the same valve entity ({entity}). Unless they also share a Pump ID or pump power sensor, ZoneFlow can't tell they're the same physical valve and won't stop them from opening it at the same time. Give one of the zones its own valve, or set a matching Pump ID on both under Configure.

init.title: Replace the sensor
init.description: The sensor {entity} used by {zone} has been offline for days. Choose a sensor to use instead, or leave it empty to stop using one (the zone then works without it).

data_description.replacement: Leave empty to remove the sensor from this zone.

init.title: Choose another phone
init.description: The phone {entity} no longer exists, so {zone} cannot send you messages. Choose another phone to send to, or leave it empty for none.

data_description.notify_entity: Leave empty to stop phone messages from this zone.

init.title: Set the flow rate by measuring
init.description: {zone} still has the example flow rate, so its watering times are guesses. Put a bucket under the emitters (or note your water meter), then run the valve for 15 minutes. Run it now?

data.run: Run the valve for 15 minutes now

data_description.run: Untick if you have already run it.

measure.title: How much water came out?
measure.description: Enter what {zone} gave in that run, the area it watered and how many minutes the valve was open.

data_description.area: Square metres (square feet on an imperial zone).

error.out_of_range: Those numbers give a flow rate this zone cannot have. Check them.

abort.zone_busy: The zone is busy. Try again in a moment.

greenhouse_sensor.title: {zone}: inside temperature sensor not working
greenhouse_sensor.description: The inside temperature sensor of zone {zone} ({entity}) has not given a usable reading for a while, so the climate control is on its failsafe: the misters and heater are off, and the vents and fans follow the Sensor Failsafe setting. Check the sensor. This clears by itself once it reports again.

greenhouse_outside_sensor.title: {zone}: outside temperature sensor not working
greenhouse_outside_sensor.description: The outside temperature sensor of zone {zone} ({entity}) has not given a usable reading for a while. Ventilation carries on from the inside readings only, so it can't check that the outside air is cooler. Check the sensor. This clears by itself once it reports again.

greenhouse_device.title: {zone}: a climate device is not responding
greenhouse_device.description: Zone {zone} switched its {devices} but they did not report the change, even after a second try. Check the device and its integration. This clears by itself once the devices respond.

greenhouse_mist_halted.title: {zone}: misting stopped
greenhouse_mist_halted.description: A mister of zone {zone} would not switch off when told to, so misting has been stopped to avoid flooding. Check the mister, then press Reset Irrigation Lock on the zone to start misting again.

greenhouse_on_backup_sensor.title: {zone}: running on the backup temperature sensor
greenhouse_on_backup_sensor.description: The main inside temperature sensor of zone {zone} ({entity}) has stopped working, so the climate control is using a backup sensor. Check the main sensor. This clears by itself once it reports again.

greenhouse_sensor_mismatch.title: {zone}: inside temperature sensors disagree
greenhouse_sensor_mismatch.description: The main inside temperature sensor of zone {zone} ({entity}) reads {main} while the backup reads {backup}, and they have been far apart for a while. One of them is probably wrong or badly placed (in direct sun, next to the heater). Check both. This clears by itself once they agree.

weather_underground_no_data.title: Weather Underground rain: no data
weather_underground_no_data.description: None of the chosen Weather Underground stations has sent a usable rain reading for {hours} hours, so zones using it act as if they had no rain gauge. Check the stations on wunderground.com, or pick others under the Weather Underground entry's Configure. This clears by itself once data returns.

greenhouse_removed.title: {zone}: its greenhouse was removed
greenhouse_removed.description: Greenhouse {greenhouse} was deleted, so {zone} is now a zone on its own. It keeps watering and keeps the greenhouse's inside sensors. To put it in another greenhouse, use the zone's Configure -> Greenhouse.

area_removed.title: {zone}: its area was removed
area_removed.description: The area {area} was deleted, so {zone} now uses a copy of the sensors it got from it. To put it in another area, use the zone's Configure -> Where is this?
